mainTopic: Whether exact precision is possible (אפשר לצמצם), and the rulings on two firstborn lambs born together: who gets which lamb, and whether the priestly gifts are owed.
overview: This amud continues the question of whether two things can ever be exactly equal (אפשר לצמצם). The question comes up because of the משנה about two firstborn lambs whose heads came out together. The גמרא first explains that רבי אליעזר simply follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that exact precision is possible. A ברייתא about an עגלה ערופה found exactly between two towns turns out to be about reading the word קרובה, not about precision. A second ברייתא, where the חכמים have the towns share one heifer with a stipulation, proves that the רבנן hold exact precision is impossible, even for things done by people. The גמרא then explains the משנה: רבי טרפון gives the כהן the better lamb, because the healthier one came out first. רבי יוחנן reads רבי עקיבא's 'משמנין' as meaning the כהן gets only the leaner lamb unless he brings proof. Next the גמרא gives the reasons of רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי on whether the owner must give the priestly gifts from the second lamb. רבי אלעזר limits רבי יוסי's exemption to cases where the כהן holds a replacement. The amud ends with a challenge from the end of the משנה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on an earlier proof by explaining that רבי אליעזר holds like רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says exact precision is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבי אליעזר) holds like רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said: it is possible to be exactly precise in things done by Heaven, and all the more so in things done by people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is blocking a proof from the previous section. It says רבי אליעזר's view tells us nothing new, because he just follows רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the גמרא tried to use רבי אליעזר to learn what the חכמים think about precision. The answer is that רבי אליעזר belongs to רבי יוסי הגלילי's camp, which holds that precision is possible. So he cannot be used to show what the other side thinks.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible to be exactly precise (two things can be perfectly equal)
In the hands of Heaven (natural events, like births)
In human hands (things people measure or do)
And all the more so

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of an argument. "He" means רבי אליעזר, who was discussed on the previous amud.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
phrases.notes: "He" refers to רבי אליעזר from the previous discussion.

phrases.english: who said: it is possible to be precise in matters of Heaven,
and all the more so in human matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a proof made earlier.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The attempt to learn the חכמים' view on precision from רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר holds like רבי יוסי הגלילי, so his view says nothing about those who disagree.

steps.title: Suggesting the heifer dispute is about precision
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא's dispute about a corpse found exactly between two towns depends on whether precision is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a dispute between תנאים: If a body was found exactly between two towns, they would not break the heifer's neck. רבי אליעזר says both towns bring two heifers. Isn't the dispute this: the תנא קמא holds precision is impossible, and רבי אליעזר holds it is possible?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about עגלה ערופה. It proposes that the two opinions there are arguing about whether exact precision is possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed reading is this. The תנא קמא brings no heifer because he thinks a body can never truly be exactly in the middle. רבי אליעזר has both towns bring heifers because he thinks it really can be exactly in the middle. If this reading holds, our question about precision would be an old dispute among תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like (a dispute of) the תנאים
Exactly lined up, precisely in the middle
Break the neck (of the עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה)
Is it not that... (introduces a proposed reading)
The first, unnamed תנא
They disagree

steps.confusionAlert: עגלה ערופה is brought by the town nearest to an unsolved murder. That is why a body exactly in the middle creates a problem.

phrases.english: Let us say it is a dispute of Tannaim:
If [the corpse] was found exactly between two towns —
they would not break [the heifer's] neck;
Rabbi Eliezer says:
both of them bring two heifers.
Is it not that they disagree about this,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם,
phrases.english: that the first Tanna holds: it is impossible to be precise,
and Rabbi Eliezer holds: it is possible to be precise?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new attempt to locate the precision question in an earlier dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That whether precision is possible is already a dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a corpse found exactly between two towns (עגלה ערופה).

steps.title: Why not bring one jointly owned heifer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the proposed reading. If precision were impossible, the towns could simply share one heifer with a stipulation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do you really think so? If the תנא קמא held that precision is impossible, why would they not break the neck at all? Let them bring one heifer as partners and stipulate!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading it just proposed. It shows that this reading does not fit the תנא קמא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If precision is impossible, then one town really is closer, and we simply do not know which one. In that case the towns could share one heifer and stipulate that it belongs to whichever town is truly nearer. Since the תנא קמא brings no heifer at all, he cannot be someone who holds precision is impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so? (introduces a rejection)
Why?
In partnership, jointly owned
And let them stipulate (make a condition)

phrases.english: And do you really think so?

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם,
phrases.english: If the first Tanna holds it is impossible to be precise,
why would they not break the neck?
Let them bring one heifer in partnership and stipulate!
phrases.notes: The stipulation: the heifer belongs to whichever town is actually nearer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading proposed in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תנא קמא holds precision is impossible.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one town is truly nearer but unknown, a shared heifer with a stipulation would work. So refusing any heifer makes no sense under that view.

steps.title: Everyone agrees precision is possible; the dispute is about "nearest"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that both תנאים agree precision is possible. They argue over whether the singular word קרובה excludes two equally near towns.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, for these תנאים, everyone agrees precision is possible. Here they argue about whether "nearest" (singular) excludes several nearest towns. The תנא קמא holds "nearest" means one, not several. רבי אליעזר holds "nearest" includes even several.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the ברייתא. The argument is about reading a word in the פסוק, not about precision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a body can lie exactly in the middle. The תנא קמא reads the singular קרובה as requiring one single nearest town, so two equally near towns bring nothing. רבי אליעזר holds the פסוק still applies when two towns are equally near, so each brings a heifer. As a result, the ברייתא cannot prove anything about whether precision is possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new explanation)
Everyone agrees
Nearest (singular), from the פסוק about עגלה ערופה
Nearest ones (plural), several equally near towns

steps.whatToRemember: The עגלה ערופה dispute is not about whether precision is possible, since everyone agrees it is. It is about whether the singular קרובה excludes two equally near towns.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the ברייתא as a source for the precision debate. The next steps (5–8) find a different source that settles the רבנן's view.

phrases.english: Rather, according to these Tannaim,
everyone agrees it is possible to be precise,
and here they disagree about "nearest" and not several nearest towns,
for the first Tanna holds: "nearest" means one, not several nearest,
and Rabbi Eliezer holds: "nearest" includes even several nearest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 3 by redefining what the dispute is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the point of dispute (from logic to reading a verse)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argue about whether precision is possible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree precision is possible. They argue whether the singular קרובה excludes two equally near towns.

steps.title: So what is the final view of the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the conclusion is about the רבנן's view on whether exact precision is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about it?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 4 left the earlier ברייתא without a proof. Now the גמרא asks what the real conclusion is about the רבנן's opinion. This short question sets up the next move, a new source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that the earlier ברייתא does not tell us the רבנן's view on צמצום, because both sides there agree precision is possible. So the question is still open. The גמרא now looks for a different source to settle it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it? (a request for the final outcome of an open question)
Exact precision, meaning two things matching perfectly

phrases.english: What is [the conclusion] about it?
phrases.notes: Asks for the רבנן's final position on whether precision is possible, even for things done by people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 4 removed the proof, so the question comes back.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the רבנן hold that exact precision is possible or impossible for things done by people?

steps.title: A ברייתא about a corpse found exactly between two towns
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין quotes רב עמרם, who cites a ברייתא. There רבי אליעזר says two heifers are brought, and the חכמים say one shared heifer is brought with a stipulation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב עמרם: It was taught: If [a corpse] was found exactly between two towns, רבי אליעזר says both towns bring two heifers. The חכמים say they bring one heifer as partners and make a stipulation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a ברייתא about עגלה ערופה. In this ברייתא, a body was found exactly in the middle between two towns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says each town brings its own heifer. The חכמים say the towns bring one heifer together and make a condition: it counts for whichever town is really closer. This condition is the key detail the גמרא will analyze next.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly aligned, precisely in the middle
Towns
The heifer whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown
In partnership, owned jointly
And they stipulate, make a condition

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Avin said that Rav Amram said:

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא נִמְצָא מְכוָּּון בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת,
phrases.english: It was taught: If [the corpse] was found exactly between two towns,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: שְׁתֵּיהֶן מְבִיאוֹת שְׁתֵּי עֲגָלוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: Both of them bring two heifers,
and the Sages say: They bring one heifer
in partnership, and they stipulate.
phrases.notes: The condition is that the heifer belongs to whichever town is truly the nearer one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם: תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question asked in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's view on whether precision is possible
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a corpse found exactly between two towns, cited by רב עמרם

steps.title: Ruling out the other ways to explain the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests each possible view of the רבנן. If precision is possible and קרובה includes several towns, two heifers should be brought. If קרובה excludes several towns, not even one should be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do the רבנן hold? If they hold precision is possible, and 'nearest' can include even several nearest towns, they should bring two heifers! And if 'nearest' means only one and not several, they should not bring even one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן must be thinking, and it knocks out the options one by one. This sets up the conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the two towns can truly be equally close. Then either both count as 'the nearest' and each should bring its own heifer, or neither counts and no heifer is needed. A single shared heifer fits neither choice. So the view that precision is possible cannot explain the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold, this is their view
Nearest (singular), the word used in the פסוק about עגלה ערופה
Nearest ones (plural)
Let them bring two

phrases.english: What do the Rabbis hold?
If the Rabbis hold that precision is possible,
and 'nearest' includes even several nearest towns, let them bring two!
And if [it means] 'nearest' but not several nearest,
they should not bring even one!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבְרִי רַבָּנַן? אִי קָסָבְרִי רַבָּנַן דְּאֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the חכמים's ruling in the ברייתא by ruling out the alternatives.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which view about precision can explain the חכמים's one shared heifer with a stipulation?

steps.title: The רבנן hold that precision is impossible, even for things done by people
steps.stepSummary: The only option left is that the רבנן hold exact precision is impossible, even for things done by people. The גמרא confirms this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that the רבנן hold precision is impossible, even for things done by people? Yes, learn it from this.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the other options failed, the גמרא concludes that the רבנן hold two things can never be exactly equal. It then confirms this with 'שמע מינה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If perfect equality cannot happen, one town really is closer, but we do not know which one. That is why the two towns share one heifer with a condition: it counts for whichever town is truly closer. The words 'even for things done by people' tell us this applies even to human-made situations, not only to natural events.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, must we not learn from this...?
It is impossible to be exactly precise
By human hands, things done by people

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, two things can never be exactly equal, even when people do them. So a corpse 'exactly in the middle' is really closer to one town, and the shared heifer with a condition solves the doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the open question about the רבנן's view on צמצום. It also gives the background for the משנה's case of two firstborns whose heads came out together: one of them really did come out first.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קָסָבְרִי רַבָּנַן:
phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from it that the Rabbis hold:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם, וַאֲפִילּוּ בִּידֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: It is impossible to be precise, even with things done by people.
Learn from it [that this is so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the only remaining conclusion after step 7 ruled out the other options.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The רבנן hold that exact precision is impossible, even for things done by people.

steps.title: Why does רבי טרפון let the כהן pick the better animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי טרפון from the משנה, who says the כהן chooses the better of the two male firstborns, and asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: He chooses for himself the better one. What is רבי טרפון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about a ewe that gave birth to two males whose heads came out at the same time. It asks why רבי טרפון gives the כהן the better one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the firstborn belongs to the כהן, and here we do not know which one came out first. So it seems strange that the כהן gets to choose the better one. The גמרא wants the logic behind this.

keyTerms.meaning: He chooses the better one for himself
What is the reason?
Firstborn male animal, which is given to the כהן

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: בּוֹרֵר לוֹ אֶת הַיָּפֶה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says: He [the priest] chooses the better one for himself.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה about two males whose heads came out together.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Tarfon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about צמצום and returns to explaining the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the כהן get the better animal when we do not know which one was born first?

steps.title: The healthier one came out first
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון assumes that the healthier, stronger lamb came out first, so it is the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: The healthy one came out first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי טרפון uses a reasonable assumption: the stronger lamb pushed out first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this assumption, the better animal is very likely the real firstborn. So giving it to the כהן is not a free choice. It is a judgment about which one was actually born first.

keyTerms.meaning: Healthy, strong
Came out first

phrases.aramaic: קָא סָבַר: הָהוּא דְּבָרִיא נָפֵק בְּרֵישָׁא.
phrases.english: He holds: That one which is healthy came out first.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָבַר: הָהוּא דְּבָרִיא נָפֵק בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי טרפון presumes the healthier lamb was born first, so it is the בכור.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: according to רבי עקיבא, the כהן takes the lean one
steps.stepSummary: On רבי עקיבא's ruling 'משמנין', רבי יוחנן says the כהן takes the leaner of the two animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'They assess', etc. רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The כהן takes the lean one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's view from the משנה. Then it brings רבי יוחנן's explanation of what that view means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we cannot know which lamb came out first, רבי יוחנן says the כהן gets only the weaker, leaner one. That is the least the owner surely owes him. This seems to be different from what the word 'משמנין' suggests, which sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They assess (literally, weigh the 'fatness' or value)
Lean, thin
Takes

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: 'They assess', etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה: 'משמנין ביניהן', they assess between them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The priest takes the lean one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַכֹּהֵן נוֹטֵל כְּחוּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next opinion in the משנה, רבי עקיבא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the כהן receives the leaner of the two animals.

steps.title: But the משנה says they assess between them
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא challenges רבי יוחנן: the משנה's words 'משמנין ביניהן' suggest that the value is divided between the כהן and the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said to רבי יוחנן: But we learned 'they assess between them'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling by pointing to the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'between them' sound like the כהן and the owner split the value, or work it out together. That does not seem to fit 'the כהן simply takes the lean one'. So the wording of the משנה seems to contradict רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned! (introduces a challenge from a משנה)
Between them

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to Rabbi Yochanan:
But we learned: 'They assess between them'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling stated in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the כהן takes the lean animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's words 'between them' suggest the value is divided, not that the כהן just takes the leaner one.

steps.title: We explained it based on the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers sharply: while you were still in בבל eating dates, we in ארץ ישראל already explained this phrase based on the later part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: While you were eating dates in בבל, we explained it from the end of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends his ruling. He says the end of the משנה shows how to read 'משמנין' correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not deny the wording. He says it must be read together with the משנה's later clause, and that clause supports giving the כהן the lean animal. The comment about eating dates is a playful jab: the matter was already worked out in ארץ ישראל long ago.

keyTerms.meaning: Unripe or poor-quality dates (a typical food of בבל)
We explained it, we interpreted it
From the latter clause, the end of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's remark about dates is not part of the legal argument. It is a lighthearted rebuke. The real answer is 'תרגימנא מסיפא': the later clause of the משנה shows how to read 'משמנין'.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַד דַּאֲכַלְתְּ כַּפְנְיָיתָא בְּבָבֶל,
phrases.english: He said to him: While you were eating dates in Babylonia,
we explained it from the latter clause.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד דַּאֲכַלְתְּ כַּפְנְיָיתָא בְּבָבֶל, תַּרְגֵּימְנָא מִסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the phrase in light of a later clause of the same משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'משמנין ביניהן' means the value is divided between the כהן and the owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: The end of the משנה shows that 'משמנין' fits with the כהן taking only the lean animal.

steps.title: Proof from the later case where one lamb died
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings proof from the סיפא of the משנה. When one lamb died, רבי עקיבא does not split anything; the owner keeps all of it. So 'משמנין' in the רישא cannot mean splitting the value.
steps.simpleTranslation: The later part of the משנה teaches: if one of the two lambs died, רבי טרפון says they split the remaining one. רבי עקיבא says the one who wants to take from his friend must bring proof. Now, if 'משמנין ביניהן' meant they split the value, then here too רבי עקיבא should say they split!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן is backing up his reading by quoting the later case in the same משנה. That case shows that רבי עקיבא never has the כהן and owner split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case where one lamb died, רבי עקיבא rules 'המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה', so the owner keeps the remaining lamb completely. If רבי עקיבא believed in splitting when unsure, he would have said to split here too. Since he does not, 'משמנין' in the first case cannot mean splitting.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a משנה or ברייתא
They divide it (split the value)
Whoever wants to take something from another person must bring proof
And if you would think (introduces a reading the גמרא is about to reject)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two תנאים here. In the case where one lamb died, it is רבי טרפון who says to split. רבי עקיבא says the owner keeps the lamb unless the כהן brings proof.

phrases.english: As the latter clause teaches:
If one of them died,
Rabbi Tarfon says: they divide it,
Rabbi Akiva says:
The one who takes from his fellow bears the burden of proof.
phrases.notes: So the owner keeps the remaining lamb.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that 'they assess between them' means they divide equally,
then here too let them divide between each other!
phrases.notes: The text shows a corrected reading in brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'later part of the משנה' that רבי יוחנן mentioned in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That 'משמנין' does not mean splitting the value between the כהן and the owner
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה, where רבי עקיבא rules that the burden of proof is on the claimant

steps.title: The true meaning of 'משמנין': the extra fat is in dispute
steps.stepSummary: 'משמנין' means the extra value, the 'fat', of the better lamb is what they argue about. The owner tells the כהן: bring proof that the fat one is the firstborn and take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'משמנין' mean? The extra fat is what is in dispute between them. The owner says to the כהן: bring proof that this one is the firstborn, and then take it.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the 'splitting' reading, רבי יוחנן gives the correct meaning of the word. This finishes his answer to רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word משמנין comes from שומן (fat). The only question is who gets the extra value of the fatter lamb. Since the כהן cannot prove that the fat one is the בכור, the owner keeps it, and the כהן gets the leaner lamb, just as רבי יוחנן said in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat, meaning the extra value of the healthier lamb
Bring proof
And take it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא there is no splitting. The owner keeps the better lamb, and the כהן gets the leaner one unless he can prove otherwise.

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'they assess' mean?
The extra fat will be in dispute between them,
for the owner says to the priest:
Bring proof that it is the firstborn, and take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading now that step 14 has ruled out the 'splitting' reading.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'משמנין' means the extra value is in dispute. The owner keeps the better lamb and the כהן takes the leaner one, which confirms רבי יוחנן's ruling.

steps.title: The משנה: the second lamb grazes, and there is a dispute about the gifts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. The second lamb, which the owner keeps, must graze until it gets a blemish, and the owner must give the priestly gifts from it. רבי יוסי exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the second lamb must graze until it gets a blemish. The owner must give the gifts from it, and רבי יוסי exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It is setting up a discussion of each side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second lamb might be the בכור, so it cannot be used until it gets a blemish. Once it is slaughtered, the question is whether the owner must give the מתנות (foreleg, jaw and stomach) that come from a regular animal. The first opinion, which is רבי מאיר, says yes; רבי יוסי says no.

keyTerms.meaning: It must graze until it gets a blemish
The priestly gifts: foreleg, jaw and stomach
Exempts

phrases.english: And the second must graze until it becomes blemished,
and it is obligated in the priestly gifts,
and Rabbi Yosei exempts it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, after the discussion of 'משמנין' has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion (רבי מאיר) says the owner must give the gifts from the second lamb; רבי יוסי says he is exempt.

steps.title: Asking for רבי מאיר's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר makes the owner give the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the first opinion in the משנה. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question arises because the second lamb is only a possible בכור. A בכור never requires gifts, so it is not obvious why the owner should owe them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The תנא behind the first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the first ruling in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the owner must give the gifts from an animal that might be a בכור

steps.title: The כהן wins either way
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the כהן has a claim either way. If the lamb is the בכור, all of it is his; if it is not, he is owed the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Because the כהן comes at him from two sides. He says to the owner: if it is a בכור, the whole thing is mine; if it is not a בכור, give me the gifts from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question about רבי מאיר. The כהן's claim works no matter what the truth is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually doubt helps the owner keep his property. Here, though, there is no possibility in which the כהן gets nothing. Either he owns the whole animal or he is owed its gifts, so at the very least the gifts must be given.

keyTerms.meaning: From two sides, meaning the כהן has a claim either way
All of it is mine
Give me

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a key idea about doubt: if a claimant wins under every possibility, the doubt does not help the defendant.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְכֹהֵן בָּא עָלָיו מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין,
phrases.english: Since the priest comes upon him from two sides,
for he says to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּכוֹר הוּא — כּוּלֵּיהּ דִּידִי הוּא,
phrases.english: If it is a firstborn, all of it is mine;

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא בְּכוֹר הוּא — הַב לִי מַתָּנוֹת מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: if it is not a firstborn, give me the gifts from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוֹאִיל וְכֹהֵן בָּא עָלָיו מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהן's claim is valid either way: the whole animal if it is a בכור, or the gifts if it is not.

steps.title: Asking for רבי יוסי's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי exempts the owner from the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason of רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: After hearing רבי יוחנן's strong argument, the גמרא asks how רבי יוסי could disagree. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's 'two sides' argument seems airtight. So the גמרא needs to know what reasoning lets רבי יוסי exempt the owner anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who exempts the owner from the gifts

phrases.english: And what is the reasoning of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the other side, now that step 18 has explained רבי מאיר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוסי exempts the owner of the second lamb from the gifts

steps.title: It is as if the כהן got the lamb and sold it back
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that, in this case, the חכמים treated the כהן as if he had acquired the second lamb too. It is as though the כהן then sold it back to the owner with its blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They treated one who did not acquire as if he did acquire. So even though the second lamb never reached the כהן's hands, it is considered as if it did, and he sold it to the Israelite with its blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives רבי יוסי's reasoning. The כהן already got one lamb, and that settles his claim on the second one, gifts included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the כהן received one of the two lambs, the arrangement is viewed as a swap. It is as if he received both and then sold the second back. So the owner can say: maybe this is the בכור, and you already got your share through the exchange. A בכור never owes gifts, so the 'two sides' argument is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: They treated one who did not acquire as one who did acquire
It reached his hands, meaning his possession
And he sold it
With its blemish

steps.confusionAlert: The כהן never actually held the second lamb. רבא is describing how the law views the situation, not something that really happened.

phrases.english: Rava said:
They rendered one who did not acquire like one who acquired,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מְטָא לִידֵיהּ
phrases.english: and even though it did not reach his possession,
it is as though it reached his possession,
and he sold it to the Israelite with its blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא עָשׂוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה כְּזוֹכֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by giving רבי יוסי's reasoning, which explains why the 'two sides' argument of רבי מאיר (step 18) does not apply in his view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהן is viewed as having acquired the second lamb and sold it back while blemished, so the owner can claim it is a בכור and exempt from gifts.

steps.title: Everyone agrees when the כהן got nothing in exchange
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that when the כהן got no replacement animal, everyone, even רבי יוסי, agrees the gifts must be given from a ספק בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Everyone agrees that in a case of a ספק בכור where the כהן has no replacement in his hands, the gifts must be given.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר limits the dispute. רבי יוסי's exemption applies only when the כהן already received one animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reason, from רבא, depends on the 'exchange': the כהן got one lamb in place of the other. If the כהן received nothing, as when a male and a female were born together, there is no exchange to rely on. Then רבי יוחנן's 'two sides' argument stands, and the gifts are owed.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
An animal that might be a firstborn
A replacement, something received in exchange

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי applies only when the כהן already got one lamb. If he got nothing, all agree the owner gives the gifts.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יוסי's exemption is not a general rule for every ספק בכור. It rests only on the 'exchange' that רבא described.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
All agree regarding an uncertain firstborn
whose replacement is not in the priest's possession,
that it is obligated in the priestly gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בִּסְפֵק בְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limits of the dispute using רבא's reasoning from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the כהן received no replacement animal, everyone agrees the owner of a ספק בכור must give the gifts.

steps.title: Why did רבי אלעזר need to say this? It seems obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who 'everyone' refers to in רבי אלעזר's statement. If it means רבי יוסי, his agreement seems obvious, because his exemption depends on the כהן holding a replacement.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אלעזר said 'everyone agrees,' whom did he mean? רבי יוסי? That's obvious! רבי יוסי only exempted the owner there, where the כהן holds a replacement animal, because the חכמים treated him as if he had acquired it. But where the כהן has no replacement, רבי יוסי would not exempt him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's statement as unnecessary. It argues that we already know from רבי יוסי's own reasoning that he would require the gifts here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 20, רבא explained that רבי יוסי exempts the owner only because the כהן already holds a replacement animal. The חכמים treated the כהן as if he had acquired this lamb too. Without a replacement, that reason disappears, so the obligation to give the gifts should obviously stand.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! Why does this need to be said?
He only exempted up to here (in this case only)
Replacement or exchange animal
One who did not acquire is treated like one who acquired

phrases.english: 'Everyone agrees': who is meant?
Rabbi Yosei? That is obvious!

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא פָטַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei only exempted there
where the replacement is in the כהן's hand,
because they treated one who did not acquire like one who acquired,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן — לָא!
phrases.english: but where there is no replacement in the כהן's hand, no (he would not exempt)!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים מַאן? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי? פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבי אלעזר's statement in Step 21, using רבא's explanation from Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement that even רבי יוסי agrees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's reason depends on a replacement being in the כהן's hand. With no replacement, his agreement follows automatically, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought רבי יוסי worried about shearing and work
steps.stepSummary: The statement is needed. Otherwise we might think רבי יוסי exempts the owner so that he won't treat the animal as fully ordinary and come to shear it or work with it. That worry would apply even without a replacement.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבי יוסי's reason is this: if you require the owner to give the gifts, he will come to shear the animal and work with it. On that view he would exempt the owner even when the כהן has no replacement. So רבי אלעזר teaches us that this is not the reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by suggesting a different possible reason for רבי יוסי. רבי אלעזר's statement rules that reason out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ספק בכור may not be shorn or worked, since it might be a בכור. If the owner gives the gifts, as from an ordinary animal, he might think it is fully ordinary and shear it or work with it. If that were רבי יוסי's worry, he would exempt the owner in every case. רבי אלעזר teaches that רבי יוסי's real reason is the replacement, so without one he agrees the gifts are owed.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
It teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)
Shearing the wool
Working with the animal
The כהן's gifts: foreleg, cheeks, and stomach

steps.confusionAlert: The shearing-and-work reason is NOT רבי יוסי's real view. It is only the mistaken idea that רבי אלעזר's statement comes to reject.

phrases.english: You might have said:
Rabbi Yosei's reason is that he holds
that if you obligate him in the gifts,
he will come to shearing and work,
phrases.notes: Both are forbidden with a possible בכור

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: even though there is no replacement in the כהן's hand,
phrases.notes: On that reasoning he would exempt even here

phrases.english: so it teaches us (that this is not so).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: the statement rejects a plausible alternative reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי exempts because of the worry about shearing and work, which applies even without a replacement
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי's reason is the replacement in the כהן's hand, so without one he agrees the gifts are owed
steps.whyThisMatters: It pins down that רבי יוסי's exemption depends on the replacement, not on a protective decree. This sets up the next challenge.

steps.title: Challenge from the end of the משנה, where רבי יוסי speaks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can say this, and begins quoting the last clause of the משנה, where רבי יוסי gives a ruling. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say this? But the end of the משנה teaches that רבי יוסי used to say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to Step 23's answer: could one really have thought רבי יוסי's reason was shearing and work? It introduces a quote from the end of the משנה, and that quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said רבי אלעזר's statement was needed because we might have thought רבי יוסי exempts even without a replacement. The גמרא now objects that רבי יוסי's own words at the end of the משנה already link his exemption to the replacement in the כהן's hand, so that mistake could not have been made. The quote itself continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really say this?
But it was taught (introduces a contradicting source)
The latter clause of the משנה

phrases.english: And can you really say this?
But the latter clause teaches,
as Rabbi Yosei would say:
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי? וְהָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against the conclusion of Step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The מהו דתימא of step 23: that, without רבי אלעזר's statement, one could have thought רבי יוסי's reason was the worry about shearing and work, so he would exempt even where no replacement is in the כהן's hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's own words in the סיפא of the משנה make the exemption depend on the replacement being in the כהן's hand. So the mistaken assumption of step 23 could never have arisen, and רבי אלעזר's statement again looks unnecessary. The quote continues on the next amud.
